perItemFindings.label: thm:primitive-endpoint-concentration
perItemFindings.one_line: `localized_empiricalGram_coercive` controls empirical matrices of the rank-one form Σ_i q(O_i) φ(O_i)φ(O_i)^T, but each planned R_{ajℓ} and Q_{ajℓ} summand is a time integral of p(t,X_i)p(t,X_i)^T and is generally not rank-one; additionally `designInv00_perturb` only bounds the (0,0) inverse entry, not the full inverse needed for the 10 coefficient learner.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan thm:primitive-endpoint-concentration/Helpers.CellConcentration: drop the claimed direct LocalizedGram and full-inverse perturbation reuse. Derive concentration for the integrated matrix-valued summands entrywise from `iid_sum_bernstein_union_bound` (or add a correctly typed local matrix-summand lemma), and supply a full operator-norm/inverse perturbation argument rather than `designInv00_perturb`.

perItemFindings.label: S5
perItemFindings.one_line: `RegularSubmodel` only stores `path`, `path_zero`, and an arbitrary mean-zero `score`; it contains no path-score/DQM/regularity relation. Thus it cannot soundly model the core's admissible semiparametric submodels or their tangent scores.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan S5 and the canonical-gradient theorem's use of `IsPathwiseGradient`/`IsTangentSpace`: define a local regular-submodel interface tying each score to its actual in-class law path (and DQM where required), then use projection packaging only if it can be restricted to that interface. As written, the library quantifies over constant paths paired with arbitrary mean-zero scores, so it cannot establish the intended canonical-gradient claim.

perItemFindings.one_line: `Causalean.Stat.Nonparametric.holder_taylor_monomial_approx` requires a symmetric closed sup-norm cube around `x0` contained in its domain (`hS`) and `h < r`; it cannot directly cover the learner's boundary/terminal cells of `[0,1]^2` under only `HolderBallStd` on that domain, so it is not a clean total fit for (C5)/(C9).
